newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-AJAX SEEK TO REDISCOVER SCORING TOUCH AGAINST SWISS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX SEEK TO REDISCOVER SCORING TOUCH AGAINST SWISS.

text.p: Early pacesetters Ajax Amsterdam and Grasshopper Zurich meet on Wednesday in Group A of the European Cup's Champions' League, with the Dutch side seeking to end a worrying goal drought.

Ajax, winners of Europe's premier club competition in 1995 and beaten finalists in 1996, have looked dramatically off form in the Dutch first division and languish in seventh place, already eight points adrift of leaders Feyenoord Rotterdam.
Transfers and injuries have decimated the team which took Ajax to European glory and won the World Club Cup but the key deficiency has been in scoring goals.
With sharpshooter Patrick Kluivert sidelined with a long-term knee injury and Nigerian international Nwankwo Kanu at Inter Milan, the Dutch champions have lost their fire power.
Seven league games have yielded only five goals, all at home. At the same stage last season Ajax had scored 27 goals and were well on their way to their 26th domestic title.
As hopes fade fast of adding a 27th, Ajax are already looking to Europe to keep their season alive.

A battling 1-0 win in Auxerre earlier this month, courtesy of Finn Jari Litmanen's 20th European goal, suggested the Dutch may have been written off too early and sets up an intriguing encounter with the Swiss who rolled over Glasgow Rangers 3-0 on the same night for their first ever Champions' League win.
Like Ajax, the Zurich club's league form does not match their European exploits.

They are currently third in the Swiss league with just one win in their last five games and will delay selection pending fitness tests on seven doubtful starters -- Mats Gren, Joel Magnin, Harald Gamperle, Tomasz Rzasa, Alain Geiger, Nestor Subiat and Kubilay Turkyilmaz who has a strained calf-muscle.
Euro 96 striker Turkyilmaz, who scored twice against Rangers and has netted five goals in 12 Swiss league games this season, has attracted the attention of Ajax, according to Dutch reports.
But Grasshopper coach Erich Vogel is adamant the player will not be allowed to leave -- at least while the side is still in Europe.
"It's not in our plans to give up our best attacker while we have an ace to play yet in the Champions' League," he said.

Ajax welcome back skipper Danny Blind from injury but fellow international defender Winston Bogarde has joined a lengthy injury list which already sidelines John Veldman, Richard Witschge, Kluivert and Peter Hoekstra.
In France a fortnight ago, coach Louis van Gaal gave five players their European debut and was rewarded with a commanding performance in which the emphasis was on defending an early lead.

But, as he brings European soccer to Ajax's new super-stadium for the first time, Van Gaal will be hoping for more fizz up front to boost his side's chances of reaching the last eight for the third year in a row.

History favours the Dutch, who beat the Swiss club 3-0 in Amsterdam at the same stage of the competition last season, although Grasshopper were the only side in the group to take a point from Ajax with a 0-0 draw in Zurich.

Ajax Amsterdam (probable) - Edwin van der Sar; Marcio Santos, Frank de Boer, Danny Blind, Martijn Reuser; Ronald de Boer, Arnold Scholten, Kiki Musampa, Marc Overmars, Jari Litmanen, Tijjani Babangida.
